claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI trip (metered, F6 shows base + distance $34.84 (24.7 km) + time $12.96, no fixed quote), so mileage deviation passes straight into the fare.
The rider was taken 24.7 km against an optimal route of 21.6 km — 3.2 km (+15%) more than necessary (F1), and the fare billed 24.7 km of metered distance (F6).

The GPS track contains one off-route segment, 09:32–09:38, in which 2.96 km were driven where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, wandering up to 974 m away from the optimal route (F3); that segment is unexplained and therefore unexempt under RD-1.

The driver cannot rely on a reroute excuse: no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window (F11), and the only congestion records are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard (F9, F10), which is not band 1 or 2 and at most is corroborative under RD-4(b).

There was no consent to the detour: the in-app chat record is complete and contains no messages at all between rider and driver (F7), so no rider message agreeing to a route change exists before the 09:32 segment start; the driver's post-trip statement that he followed his GPS (F8) is a claim, not consent.

Because the deviation is unexempt on a metered RydeTAXI trip, the refund is the unexempt segment's extra distance × the trip's per-km rate: the fare fact prices distance at $1.41/km (F4, F6), so 2.96 km × $1.41 = $4.17 (rounded to the cent), which is the metered overcharge for that segment.
A violation of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty is established against the driver (F1, F3), which is the record the rider asks the tribunal to enter alongside the refund.

No account flag on the driver is requested: the driver's 90-day profile shows 2 disputes but route upheld = 0 (F14), so the RD-6 repeated-route-deviation predicate (a prior upheld route dispute) is not met; F14 is offered only as context and is not used to decide the detour.

weaknesses: The off-route segment extra (2.96 km, F3) is less than the total excess over the optimal route (3.2 km, F1), and part of the remaining ~0.24 km may be map-matching residual (RD-2 says residuals up to 0.25 km are not refunded) — the other side will argue the claim is overstated if we ask for 3.2 km.
The detour amount we can claim is only $4.17, not the $8.23 or similar figures suggested by the app's 22 km vs meter 25 km framing; the rider's complaint will have to be scaled down.

The driver will lean on F8 ("I followed my GPS; it rerouted me") and F9/F10 (band 4 congestion on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) to argue a legitimate reroute, and F2 (+21.4 min) shows the trip really was slower than estimated, which supports a congestion narrative.
The rider's own 90-day record shows 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F13), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of fee complaints.
The passenger waited until after the trip to raise this; there is no contemporaneous chat complaint (F7), which weakens any argument that the rider objected in real time.

The refund comes to you as a Ryde voucher. Nothing else changes for you, and no further action is needed on your side.
